scope.title: Shared capability contract
scope.boundary: Metadata and command behavior have executable observations; capability choice, useful outputs and evidence judgment need review.

initial_state: A private skill directory has name/description frontmatter, one title and Expected output. It has no resources or readability opt-in.
For negative variants validate the unchanged baseline first, then alter only the named field.
A private readable package explicitly selects schema-version skill-readability-v1, version 1.0.0, a complete Workflow role and fillable Output skeleton.
Validate before each named mutation; no historical skill version is selected.
Run the trusted skill-validator command in a fresh temporary working directory with an isolated PATH, synthetic runtime trap scripts and no RigorLoop checkout prerequisites in that directory.

Use the Review fixture basis in the strategy plus this case’s concrete facts and counterexample. Resolve every actual instruction and authority claim to the exact current owner/body/triggered resources.
Materialize a fresh private review packet for each variant. F0/F1/F2, G0/G1/G2 and S0/S1 are synthetic byte-identity labels; an actual assessment records inspected identities.
Inspect proposed decisions, outputs and prohibited side effects without running an agent or writing production, workflow records, hosted CI or publication state.

cases.title: Minimal portable package needs no artificial resource section
cases.risk: A universal layout rejects a legitimate package with no resources.

conditions: Keep the valid-basic fixture free of packaged resources and readability opt-in.

when: Invoke the public validator on that package.
then: Exit zero with a canonical-integrity result; no resource-map or absent-resource section is required.

cases.title: Required common fields have attributable diagnostics
cases.risk: A malformed entrypoint is accepted or rejected only for an unrelated fixture defect.

conditions: Start from one passing package for each independently named omission.

when: Remove only the named field or heading, then invoke validation.
then: Exit nonzero and identify the missing name, description, single top-level title or Expected output section.

gaps: Existing negative fixtures assert the intended diagnostics, but these methods do not establish the same passing fixture before each omission.

cases.title: Readability vocabulary rejects unknown values before consistency
cases.risk: An unknown schema or stage is treated as an absent optional rule.

conditions: Use the valid-pilot representation. For schema precedence combine an unknown schema with a missing Output skeleton; for the stage partition change only the stage.

when: Validate the baseline, apply the selected fault, and inspect the diagnostic set.
then: Unknown schema reports schema-version must be 'skill-readability-v1' before attempting that schema's internal consistency checks.
Unknown workflow stage is rejected with its closed-vocabulary diagnostic.

gaps: Existing fixtures cover unknown values, but do not exercise the competing schema inconsistency and exact early-return observation.

cases.title: Output aid has fillable structure
cases.risk: A skill passes with no usable output shape.

conditions: Keep the role and metadata valid; remove the Output skeleton or replace its placeholders with fixed example text.

then: Reject a missing skeleton and reject a skeleton with no fillable placeholders. This check says nothing about the completeness of an emitted artifact.

gaps: The separate negative fixtures do not prove a single valid baseline before each defining mutation.

cases.title: Description limit is a real ordered boundary
cases.risk: Only an obviously overlong description is tested, leaving the allowed edge ambiguous.

conditions: Use otherwise identical published-design packages with descriptions of 1023, 1024 and 1025 characters.

when: Run the public validator for each length.
then: Accept 1023 and 1024; reject 1025 with description must be 1024 characters or fewer.

gaps: The linked method tests an overlong fixture; just-below and at-limit acceptance are not asserted there.

cases.title: Generated mirrors cannot become authored authority
cases.risk: A validator result from generated output substitutes for canonical source validation.

conditions: Select the repository generated .codex/skills path as an authored-source input.

then: Reject with generated output path must not be used as authored source of truth.

cases.title: Canonical integrity does not invoke target agents
cases.risk: A structural check silently executes an installed target agent or needs it to pass.

conditions: Use the real proposal and proposal-review package paths. Compare a PATH without target tools and one with trap executables.

when: Run validation from the temporary directory with the trusted Python executable.
then: Both runs succeed with two one-skill results and empty stderr; the target-invoked marker never appears. This demonstrates tool independence, not agent behavior.

cases.title: Descriptions distinguish a capability and its near misses
cases.risk: Discovery metadata routes a request into a neighboring capability with different authority.

conditions: On separate requests ask to draft a direction, revise a settled Design, independently review that Design, or prepare a PR description. The user has not authorized publishing or implementing the outputs. Use the current description alone for initial selection.

when: Compare the selected capability and proposed output for each request with the complete body and required aid. Include a candidate that selects Design authorship for the independent-review request.
then: The requests resolve to Proposal, Design, Design Review and PR preparation respectively. The authorship-for-review candidate fails the independent-judgment boundary; none of the four requests grants publication or automatic implementation. Detailed artifact completeness stays with its child owner.

gaps: Perform this procedure against the exact selected package and record the independent assessment; text assertions do not establish this outcome.

cases.title: Bounded evidence expands when the claim needs it
cases.risk: A short excerpt hides conflicting authority and is still reported as sufficient.

conditions: A synthetic request asks whether the complete workflow permits writes. The first packet excerpts only an Inspect job with read-only permissions; the available full file also contains a Deploy job with write permission. A control packet contains the complete one-job read-only workflow.

when: Inspect evidence selection and the proposed whole-workflow conclusion for each packet. Compare a report claiming read-only operation from the first excerpt with one that obtains the complete relevant job/permission context.
then: Expand the incomplete packet before making the whole-workflow claim and report the omitted Deploy write permission. The complete one-job control supports the bounded read-only conclusion without unrelated file reads. A concise report that hides the material write permission fails the observation; output caps cannot suppress findings or actual command failures.

gaps: Perform this procedure against the exact selected package and record the independent assessment; text assertions do not establish this outcome.

cases.title: Evidence requests and examples remain public-safe
cases.risk: A skill demands raw credentials or machine-local private state to establish a claim.

conditions: Use a fictional failed check report with error code E_CONFIG, relevant key timeout_seconds, a TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER value and an unrelated home-directory value. The latter two are unnecessary to reproduce the reported missing-key fault.

when: Compare a proposed request for E_CONFIG and the redacted relevant configuration with one requesting the entire environment or embedding TOKEN_PLACEHOLDER in the report as if it were required evidence.
then: Only the relevant safe configuration and diagnostic are requested or reported; the full environment and credential value are omitted. All fixture values are synthetic. Stored role labels and successful package checks grant no execution authority.

gaps: Perform this procedure against the exact selected package and record the independent assessment; text assertions do not establish this outcome.
